rationale: C08 is a highly specific predecessor template for the child: both concern a named federal official approaching compulsory retirement under the same Civil Service Retirement Act, use essentially identical two-recital language, and lead into the same exemption mechanism. The adaptation principally substitutes the official, office, dates, and exemption period. C19 and C13 are also strong members of the same drafting family, but C08 is closest in wording, sequence, and temporal proximity.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS Hugh H. Bennett ... will, during the month of April 1951 become subject to compulsory retirement for age under the provisions of the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, unless exempted therefrom by Executive order
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS Paul A. Walker ... will, during the month of January 1951, become subject to compulsory retirement for age under the provisions of the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, unless exempted therefrom by Executive order
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive near-verbatim recital establishing the named official's impending retirement and the Executive-order exception.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that the said person be exempted from such compulsory retirement as provided below
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that the said person be exempted from such compulsory retirement as provided below
shared_material.explanation: The public-interest finding is verbatim and occupies the same position immediately before the operative transition.

shared_material.child_excerpt: NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me ... I hereby exempt the said Hugh H. Bennett from compulsory retirement for age
shared_material.explanation: Although the supplied C08 text truncates the operative provision, its title and preceding recitals show the same sequence and exemption machinery, strongly supporting use as a concrete drafting template.
